name: Arcturus
tagline: The brightest star of the northern sky — an orange giant racing through the galactic halo.
history: Arcturus is the brightest star in the northern celestial hemisphere — an orange giant swollen to 25 times the Sun's girth as it burns through its helium-rich years. Its high speed marks it as a visitor from the galactic thick disk, possibly debris from a dwarf galaxy the Milky Way devoured long ago. It has guided Polynesian navigators to Hawaii, lit the 1933 World's Fair via a photoelectric cell, and in ~4,000 years it will drift out of naked-eye reach entirely.
